lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Rounding to estimate
lessons.intention: We are learning to round to the nearest 10 and 100 to estimate and check answers.
criteria: I can round whole numbers to the nearest 10 and 100.
I can use rounding or doubling to estimate an answer.
I can check if my answer is sensible.

steps.start: Is 48 nearer 40 or 50? Show it on a number line.
steps.teach: Use a number line to round 2-digit numbers to 10, then 3-digit numbers to 100. Model estimating 38 + 41 as 40 + 40, then working it out and comparing.
steps.check: Round 67 and 352. Estimate 29 + 52, then check.

lessons.home: Round prices in the shop to estimate the total.
lessons.vocab: round, nearest, estimate, about, check, sensible
lessons.understand: Why would you round before you work it out?
lessons.lookFor: Uses rounding to check whether an answer is sensible.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Place value to 1000
lessons.intention: We are learning what each digit is worth in numbers to 1000.
criteria: I can read, write and order numbers to 1000.
I know zero holds a place, as in 405.
I can say what each digit is worth, as in 867 = 800 + 60 + 7.

steps.start: Make 34 with tens and ones. How many tens? How many ones?
steps.teach: Use hundreds, tens and ones (blocks or place value cards) to build 3-digit numbers. Show 405 and why the zero matters. Order four 3-digit numbers.
steps.practise: Tens and ones, then Hundreds, tens and ones.
steps.check: What is the 6 worth in 263? Write 'four hundred and nine' in digits.

lessons.home: Read big numbers on signs and prices together.
lessons.vocab: digit, place, value, hundreds, tens, ones, zero
lessons.understand: What is the 4 worth in 346? What if it moved to the hundreds?
lessons.lookFor: Explains the value of a digit depends on its place.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Counting in 2s, 5s, 10s and 100s
lessons.intention: We are learning to count forwards and backwards in steps.
criteria: I can count forwards and backwards in 2s, 5s and 10s from any number to 1000.
I can count in 100s.
I can spot the pattern in the steps.

steps.start: Count in 10s from 0, then from 3 (3, 13, 23…).
steps.teach: Use a hundred square to show counting in 2s, 5s and 10s. Count back too. Count in 100s from 50.
steps.check: Count on in 5s from 35. Count back in 2s from 20.

lessons.home: Count in 2s using pairs of socks or shoes.
lessons.vocab: count on, count back, steps, pattern, multiple
lessons.understand: What do you notice about numbers when you count in 5s?
lessons.lookFor: Spots the pattern (they end in 0 or 5) and uses it to continue or check.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Adding and subtracting within 20
lessons.intention: We are learning to add and subtract quickly within 20.
criteria: I know number bonds to 10 and 20.
I can add and subtract within 20 using what I know.
I know addition can be done in any order, as in 6 + 3 = 3 + 6.

steps.start: Quick-fire bonds to 10: 7 and ? make 10.
steps.teach: Use a bead string or ten frames. Show bridging through 10: 8 + 5 = 8 + 2 + 3. Show 6 + 3 = 3 + 6. Use 'I know 7 + 3 = 10, so 17 + 3 = 20'.
steps.practise: Number bonds to 20, Adding within 20, Taking away within 20.
steps.check: Ask 9 + 6, 15 − 7 and 13 + ? = 20, and how they worked it out.

lessons.home: Play a quick bonds game in the car: I say 6, you say 4.
lessons.vocab: add, subtract, sum, total, difference, bond, bridge
lessons.understand: If 8 + 6 = 14, what else do you know?
lessons.lookFor: Uses the fact to find others: 6 + 8 = 14, 14 − 6 = 8, 14 − 8 = 6.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Adding and subtracting to 1000
lessons.intention: We are learning to add and subtract 3-digit numbers.
criteria: I can add and subtract multiples of 10 and 100 to and from numbers to 1000.
I can add and subtract 3-digit numbers.
I can use the inverse to check.

steps.teach: Model partitioning: 253 + 125 = 200 + 100, 50 + 20, 3 + 5. Then a written method. Check 378 − 125 = 253 by adding back.
steps.practise: Adding and taking away bigger numbers.
steps.check: Work out 436 + 251 and 587 − 230, and check one with the inverse.

lessons.home: Add up two prices or two distances from a map.
lessons.vocab: add, subtract, partition, inverse, check
lessons.understand: How could you check your answer?
lessons.lookFor: Uses the inverse (adds back) or an estimate to check, and explains why the check works.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Multiplication facts: 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10
lessons.intention: We are learning to work out and remember multiplication facts.
criteria: I can work out multiplication facts using repeated addition, groups and arrays.
I can recall facts for the 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 times tables.

steps.start: Count in 5s to 50 on your fingers.
steps.teach: Build arrays with counters: 3 rows of 4. Write it as 4 + 4 + 4 and 3 × 4, then turn it to show 4 × 3. Link doubles to the 2 and 4 times tables.
steps.practise: 2, 5 and 10 times tables, then 3 and 4 times tables.
steps.check: Show an array: write two multiplication facts. Ask 4 × 5 and 3 × 6.

lessons.home: Spot arrays at home: egg boxes, muffin trays, windows.
lessons.vocab: multiply, times, groups of, lots of, array, product
lessons.understand: How could 2 × 5 help you work out 4 × 5?
lessons.lookFor: Uses doubling or facts they know to find a new fact, rather than counting from the start.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Division: sharing and grouping
lessons.intention: We are learning to divide by sharing and grouping.
criteria: I can divide by sharing equally and by making equal groups.
I can use multiplication facts to divide.
I know division undoes multiplication.

steps.start: Share 12 counters between 3 people. How many each?
steps.teach: Show 12 ÷ 3 two ways: sharing into 3 groups, and making groups of 3. Link to 3 × 4 = 12. Try a remainder: 13 ÷ 3.
steps.check: Ask 20 ÷ 5 and 18 ÷ 2, and which times table fact helps.

lessons.home: Share snacks fairly between the family.
lessons.vocab: divide, share, equal groups, shared equally, remainder
lessons.understand: Here is 12 ÷ 3. Show it as sharing, then as grouping.
lessons.lookFor: Can show both and knows the answer is the same.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Multiplying and dividing by 10 and 100
lessons.intention: We are learning to multiply and divide whole numbers by 10 and 100.
criteria: I can multiply and divide whole numbers by 10 and 100.
I can explain how the digits move.

steps.start: What is 10 lots of 3? 10 lots of 30?
steps.teach: Use a place value grid. Show 23 × 10 = 230: the digits move one place left. ×100 moves two places. Dividing moves them right.

lessons.home: How many 10p coins make £3? How many pence in £5?
lessons.vocab: multiply, divide, place, digit, ten times
lessons.understand: What happens to the digits when you multiply by 10?
lessons.lookFor: Says the digits move one place bigger, rather than just "add a zero".

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Solving two-step problems
lessons.intention: We are learning to choose what to do in a problem and solve it in two steps.
criteria: I can decide which calculation a problem needs.
I can solve two-step problems.
I can check my answer makes sense.

steps.start: Tell a one-step story: 5 apples, 3 more. Now add a second step: then 2 are eaten.
steps.teach: Read a problem together. Underline the important numbers. Draw a bar model or picture. Decide step 1 and step 2. Check with an estimate.
steps.practise: Missing numbers and signs, then make up a two-step problem for the tutor to solve.
steps.check: Sam has 24 stickers, gets 10 more and gives away 8. How many now?

lessons.home: Make up shopping problems: two things, then change.
lessons.vocab: problem, calculate, step, total, left, more, fewer
lessons.understand: Before you work it out: what are the two steps, and why that order?
lessons.lookFor: Explains which operation each step needs and why.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: What fractions are
lessons.intention: We are learning to name, write and compare fractions.
criteria: I can explain what a fraction is using pictures or objects.
I know the more equal parts, the smaller each part.
I can write fractions like ½, ⅔ and ⅝, and say what the numerator and denominator mean.
I can compare fractions and place them on a number line.

steps.start: Fold a paper strip in half, then quarters, then eighths. What happens to the parts?
steps.teach: Use fraction strips. Write ½, ¼, ⅛ and show which is biggest. Explain numerator (parts we have) and denominator (equal parts in the whole). Place ½ and ¼ on a 0–1 number line.
steps.check: Which is bigger, ⅓ or ⅕? Show ¾ of a shape.

lessons.home: Cut a pizza or cake into equal parts and name the fractions.
lessons.vocab: fraction, half, quarter, third, numerator, denominator, equal parts
lessons.understand: Which is bigger, one half or one quarter of the same pizza? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Explains more equal parts means each part is smaller.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Fractions of amounts and equivalent fractions
lessons.intention: We are learning to find a fraction of a number and to spot fractions that are the same.
criteria: I can find a fraction of an amount using division, as in ¼ of 12.
I can show simple equivalent fractions, as in ½ = 2/4.

steps.start: Share 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. What is ¼ of 12?
steps.teach: Link ¼ of 20 to 20 ÷ 4. Then use fraction strips to show ½ = 2/4 = 4/8.
steps.practise: Halves, quarters and thirds, then Equivalent fractions.
steps.check: Ask ⅓ of 15 and draw a picture to show ½ = 3/6.

lessons.home: Find half or a quarter of a bag of pasta shapes.
lessons.vocab: fraction of, share, equivalent, same as
lessons.understand: How do you find a quarter of 20? Why does that work?
lessons.lookFor: Links finding a quarter to sharing into 4 equal groups.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Paying and change within £10
lessons.intention: We are learning to pay for things and work out change.
criteria: I know all coins and notes to £20.
I can write amounts correctly, as in 149p = £1·49.
I can pay for things and work out change within £10.
I know things can be paid for with cards and phones.

steps.start: Make £1 in three different ways with coins.
steps.teach: Write prices both ways (75p, £0·75). Total two items. Count on to find change from £5 or £10 (from £3·60: 40p makes £4, then £1 makes £5).
steps.check: A book costs £3·45. What change from £5?

lessons.home: Let your child work out the change when you pay.
lessons.vocab: pounds, pence, total, change, cost, note, card
lessons.understand: You pay with 10p for something that costs 7p. How much change? How did you work it out?
lessons.lookFor: Counts on from the cost to the amount paid, or takes away, and explains which.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Half past, quarter past and quarter to
lessons.intention: We are learning to tell the time to the quarter hour.
criteria: I can tell half past, quarter past and quarter to on analogue and digital clocks.
I can use am and pm.
I know 24-hour times are used on phones and computers.

steps.start: Show o'clock times and read them.
steps.teach: Show the clock face split into quarters. Move the minute hand: quarter past, half past, quarter to. Show the matching digital times (2:15, 2:30, 2:45). Talk about am and pm.
steps.practise: Telling the time, then Digital time.
steps.check: Set quarter to 4 on a clock. What is 7:30 on an analogue clock?

lessons.home: Ask your child the time at quarter past, half past and quarter to.
lessons.vocab: quarter past, half past, quarter to, am, pm, analogue, digital
lessons.understand: Why is the hour hand between two numbers at half past?
lessons.lookFor: Knows the hour hand moves on through the hour, not just the minute hand.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Calendars, dates and how long
lessons.intention: We are learning to use calendars and work out how long things take.
criteria: I can write the date in words and numbers.
I can use a calendar to plan.
I know seconds in a minute, minutes in an hour, hours in a day, days in each month and in a year.
I can choose and use a timer.

steps.start: What is today's date? Write it two ways.
steps.teach: Use a calendar to find birthdays and count days between. Learn the time facts. Use a timer: how many star jumps in 30 seconds?
steps.check: How many days in June? How many minutes in an hour? What is the date one week from today?

lessons.home: Put family birthdays on a calendar and count down.
lessons.vocab: date, calendar, month, season, minute, hour, second, timer
lessons.understand: How long is it from Monday to Thursday? How do you know?
lessons.lookFor: Counts the gaps (days passing), not the days named.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Measuring with rulers, scales and jugs
lessons.intention: We are learning to estimate and measure in standard units.
criteria: I can estimate length, height, weight and capacity.
I can measure with rulers, metre sticks, scales and jugs to the nearest unit.
I can make simple conversions, as in 1 m 58 cm = 158 cm.
I can read scales, including halves.

steps.start: Estimate how long a pencil is in cm. Measure it.
steps.teach: Show starting a ruler at 0. Weigh fruit in grams, measure water in ml. Read a jug scale with ½ litre marked. Convert 1 m 20 cm to 120 cm.
steps.check: Measure a book in cm. Read a scale at 250 ml.

lessons.home: Bake together, measuring grams and millilitres.
lessons.vocab: estimate, measure, centimetre, metre, gram, kilogram, millilitre, litre, scale
lessons.understand: Why do we use centimetres instead of hand spans?
lessons.lookFor: Explains standard units give the same answer whoever measures.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Area by counting squares
lessons.intention: We are learning to find area by counting squares.
criteria: I can estimate and count squares to find the area of a shape, to the nearest half square.
I can make shapes with a given area.
I know different shapes can have the same area.

steps.start: How many squares cover this sticky note?
steps.teach: Draw shapes on squared paper. Count whole squares, then pair up halves. Make two different shapes with an area of 6 squares.
steps.practise: Draw three shapes with an area of 8 squares on squared paper.
steps.check: Count the area of a shape with some half squares.

lessons.home: Count the tiles on a floor or wall to find its area.
lessons.vocab: area, square, cover, half square
lessons.understand: Can two different shapes have the same area?
lessons.lookFor: Yes: area is how many squares are covered, not what the shape looks like.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Number patterns and rules
lessons.intention: We are learning to continue number patterns and explain the rule.
criteria: I can continue and make repeating patterns with shapes and symbols.
I can describe patterns in tables and the hundred square.
I can continue a number sequence and say its rule.

steps.start: 2, 4, 6, 8… what comes next? What is the rule?
steps.teach: Show sequences that add, subtract, double and halve. Find the rule and the next two numbers. Colour the 5 times table on a hundred square.
steps.check: Continue 30, 27, 24… and say the rule.

lessons.home: Make up a number pattern for someone at home to solve.
lessons.vocab: pattern, sequence, rule, next, double, halve
lessons.understand: What's the rule? What will the 10th number be?
lessons.lookFor: States the rule in words and uses it to predict, without listing every number.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Equals, greater than and missing numbers
lessons.intention: We are learning to compare numbers and find missing numbers.
criteria: I can use =, ≠, < and > correctly.
I know the equals sign means both sides balance.
I can find a missing number, as in □ + 17 = 30.

steps.start: Which is bigger, 45 or 54? Show it with < or >.
steps.teach: Use a balance picture: 8 + 2 = 5 + 5. Then □ + 6 = 15 and □ × 6 = 30, using number facts and the inverse.
steps.check: Fill in 23 □ 32 and □ − 8 = 12.

lessons.home: Make balance puzzles with coins.
lessons.vocab: equals, not equal to, less than, greater than, balance, missing
lessons.understand: What does = mean in 7 + 3 = 6 + 4?
lessons.lookFor: Explains both sides are worth the same, not "the answer comes next".

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Describing 2D shapes and 3D objects
lessons.intention: We are learning to name and describe shapes and objects.
criteria: I can name and sort 2D shapes and 3D objects in any size or way round.
I can use side, face, edge, vertex, base and angle.
I can find 2D shapes in 3D objects.
I can make a tiling pattern with two shapes.

steps.start: Show a triangle upside down: is it still a triangle?
steps.teach: Count faces, edges and vertices of a cube and a cylinder. Find the 2D faces of 3D objects. Tile with squares and triangles.
steps.check: How many faces, edges and vertices on a cuboid?

lessons.home: Find cuboids, cylinders and spheres in the kitchen.
lessons.vocab: side, face, edge, vertex, base, angle, tiling
lessons.understand: How is a cube different from a square?
lessons.lookFor: Knows a cube is 3D with faces, edges and corners, and its faces are squares.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Turns, right angles and compass points
lessons.intention: We are learning to describe turns and directions.
criteria: I can describe full, half and quarter turns, clockwise and anticlockwise.
I know a right angle is 90°.
I can use North, South, East and West.
I can find right angles in shapes and around me.

steps.start: Stand up: make a quarter turn clockwise, then a half turn.
steps.teach: Make a right-angle checker by folding paper. Find right angles in the room. Mark N, S, E, W on the walls and give directions.
steps.check: Face North, turn a quarter turn clockwise: which way now?

lessons.home: Give directions on a walk: turn left, quarter turn right.
lessons.vocab: turn, clockwise, anticlockwise, right angle, North, South, East, West
lessons.understand: If you face north and make a quarter turn clockwise, which way do you face?
lessons.lookFor: Says east, and can show the turn with their body or a pointer.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Grid references and symmetry
lessons.intention: We are learning to use grid references and to make symmetrical designs.
criteria: I know where grid references are used.
I can find and give two-figure grid references.
I can find symmetry in pictures, nature and shapes.
I can make a design with more than one line of symmetry.

steps.start: Look at a simple map with a grid. Where is the park?
steps.teach: Draw a 5 × 5 grid with letters along and numbers up. Place items and name their squares (along the corridor, then up the stairs). Fold shapes to find lines of symmetry.
steps.practise: Play a grid hide-and-seek: hide treasure in a square and guess each other's.
steps.check: Which square is the tree in? Draw the other half of a symmetrical pattern.

lessons.home: Look at a street map together and find places by their squares.
lessons.vocab: grid, reference, along, up, symmetry, line of symmetry
lessons.understand: Why does the order of a grid reference matter?
lessons.lookFor: Explains B3 and 3B point to different places if the order is swapped: across first, then up.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Collecting and showing data
lessons.intention: We are learning to collect, sort and show data, and answer questions about it.
criteria: I can answer questions using charts, bar graphs and tables.
I can collect data with a survey or tally.
I can show data in bar graphs, tables, Carroll diagrams and Venn diagrams.
I can give a graph a title, labels and a sensible scale.

steps.start: What is the favourite pet of people you know?
steps.teach: Collect answers with a tally. Draw a bar graph with a title, labelled axes and a scale going up in 2s. Sort numbers in a Venn diagram (even / more than 10).
steps.check: Ask three questions about a bar graph, including one about the difference between two bars.

lessons.home: Do a family survey and make a chart.
lessons.vocab: data, survey, tally, bar graph, table, axis, scale, Venn diagram, Carroll diagram
lessons.understand: What question could someone answer from your chart?
lessons.lookFor: Asks and answers a question the data really shows, such as which is most popular.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: How likely is it?
lessons.intention: We are learning to describe how likely things are.
criteria: I can use likely, unlikely, certain, uncertain, possible, impossible, fair and unfair.
I can use what I know to predict how likely something is.

steps.start: Will it snow tomorrow? Will the sun rise tomorrow?
steps.teach: Put events on a line from impossible to certain. Is a game with one red and five blue counters fair?
steps.check: Give three events to place on the likelihood line, with reasons.

lessons.home: Talk about the weather forecast: how likely is rain?
lessons.vocab: likely, unlikely, certain, possible, impossible, fair, unfair, chance
lessons.understand: Is it impossible or just unlikely that it will snow tomorrow? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Explains the difference: unlikely can still happen, impossible can't.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Numbers in life, work and history
lessons.intention: We are learning how numbers are used in the world and in the past.
criteria: I can talk about how numbers are used in learning, life and work.
I can explore a number system from history, such as Roman numerals.

steps.start: Where did you see numbers today?
steps.teach: List jobs that use numbers. Show Roman numerals I to XX on clocks and old buildings. Write today's day number in Roman numerals.
steps.practise: Write five numbers in Roman numerals and five jobs that use maths.
steps.check: What is XIV? Name a job that uses measuring.

lessons.home: Spot Roman numerals on clocks, films or buildings.
lessons.vocab: number system, Roman numerals
lessons.understand: Where have you seen numbers used today? What were they for?
lessons.lookFor: Gives real examples and what the number told someone (time, price, a bus number).
